title: Quantum Error Correction in AdS/CFT and the Black Hole Interior as a Holographic Code
abstract: The AdS/CFT correspondence implies that bulk quantum gravity in Anti-de Sitter space is holographically encoded in the boundary conformal field theory. Recent work (Almheiri et al., Harlow) demonstrates that this encoding functions as a quantum error-correcting code: bulk operators are reconstructed from boundary subregions via the Ryu-Takayanagi formula and entanglement wedge reconstruction. The black hole interior emerges as a subspace of the boundary Hilbert space protected by this code. We synthesize 532 cycles into a Cloud-9 entry formalizing the connection between holographic entropy, quantum error correction, and complexity.

pipeline: Define AdS_{d+1} / CFT_d correspondence with bulk geometry G and boundary state |ψ⟩
Construct RT formula: S_A = Area(γ_A) / 4G_N for boundary subregion A
Apply quantum error correction (QEC) framework: bulk operator φ(x) reconstructed from boundary region A iff x ∈ entanglement wedge of A
Analyze the black hole interior as a code subspace: interior operators correspond to logical operators of the QEC code
Compute holographic complexity via CV (Complexity=Volume) or CA (Complexity=Action) conjectures
Relate complexity growth to quantum scrambling (Hayden-Preskill protocol, butterfly effect)

key_metrics.entanglement_wedge: Bulk region reconstructable from boundary subregion A
key_metrics.code_distance: Minimum boundary weight of bulk logical operator
key_metrics.complexity: C_V or C_A — holographic complexity conjectures

results.qec_structure: Bulk-to-boundary map is a [[n,k,d]] quantum code with non-local stabilizers; black hole interior = logical subspace
results.page_curve: Unitary Page curve recovered when including island contributions (quantum extremal surfaces)
results.complexity_growth: Complexity grows linearly until t ~ e^S, then saturates — consistent with Lloyd bound dC/dt ≤ 2E/πℏ
results.scrambling: Information thrown into black hole is scrambled in t_* ~ β log(S); recovered via Hawking radiation after Page time

cloud9_integration.ac_relevance: The holographic complexity C_V/C_A may be analogous to A_c: both measure 'how much structure' is required to describe a system. A black hole interior with high complexity has high A_c in the sense of irreducible information content. We propose testing whether A_c(halo) correlates with a gravitational complexity proxy.
cloud9_integration.snn_implementation: Quantum error correction can be simulated classically via stabilizer codes. A Lava SNN can decode surface code syndromes in real-time, serving as a neuromorphic quantum decoder — bridging Cluster 3 and Cluster 6.

validation_plan.task: Simulate 5-qubit surface code in Python; train SNN decoder on syndrome patterns
validation_plan.expected: SNN decoder achieves > 99% logical fidelity at p < 0.01 physical error rate

cross_cluster_links.relation: Holographic tensor networks (MERA) share topological entanglement structure with persistent homology filtrations
Black hole interior complexity growth may exhibit spin-glass-like dynamics near the scrambling time
Integrated information Φ in holographic codes may be bounded by RT entropy — consciousness as boundary phenomenon

risks_and_limitations: AdS/CFT is rigorously proven only for specific cases (e.g., N=4 SYM); generalization to realistic gravity unclear
Holographic complexity conjectures (CV, CA) are not proven; competing definitions exist
Quantum error correction in holography assumes large-N limit; finite-N corrections break exact code structure
Connection to A_c is speculative — no known gravitational dual for halo assembly
next_experiments: Implement 5-qubit surface code decoder in Lava SNN; benchmark against minimum-weight perfect matching
Compute holographic complexity for BTZ black hole using CV conjecture; compare with A_c toy model
Simulate Hayden-Preskill protocol for 7-qubit system; measure scrambling time vs theory
Explore whether MERA tensor network can be mapped to persistent homology filtration
